expectedText:
LIVE SCAN / DOJ FINGERPRINT BACKGROUND CHECK — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Corp.

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Live Scan / Department of Justice (DOJ) fingerprint-based criminal history clearance system — a state-administered process distinct from the private consumer-reporting-agency background checks addressed elsewhere in this corpus (federal Fair Credit Reporting Act, California's Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act, and California's Fair Chance Act pre-offer inquiry restrictions). Live Scan clearance is required, not merely permitted, for certain licensed or regulated positions, and it is run through the state Department of Justice and, for some requests, the federal Bureau of Investigation, rather than through a private consumer reporting agency. This document states facts about the general statutory framework authorizing fingerprint-based DOJ background checks (Penal Code § 11105.3) and two sector-specific mandates independently verified for this document — childcare facility licensing (Health & Safety Code § 1596.871) and intermediate care facilities for the developmentally disabled (Health & Safety Code § 1265.5) — regarding Jordan Lee's prospective role with Acme Corp. It does not identify every occupation or sector subject to a Live Scan requirement, and it does not tell Acme Corp. or Jordan Lee whether Live Scan clearance applies to this particular position or what to do about any particular clearance result.

WHAT LIVE SCAN IS
"Live Scan" refers to the electronic fingerprint-capture technology the California Department of Justice uses to process criminal history background checks, as opposed to older ink-and-paper fingerprint cards. State law describes the Legislature's support for "the use of the fingerprint live-scan technology... for fully automating the processing of fingerprints and other data," a system also referred to as the California Crime Information Intelligence System (CAL-CII). Once live-scan technology is operational for a given licensing program, an individual is required to obtain either a criminal record clearance from the Department of Justice or a criminal record exemption from the relevant state department before that individual's initial presence in the regulated facility or role.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "the Legislature supports the use of the fingerprint live-scan technology, as identified in the long-range plan of the Department of Justice, for fully automating the processing of fingerprints and other data by the year 1999, otherwise known as the California Crime Information Intelligence System (CAL-CII) to be used for applicant fingerprints. Therefore, when live-scan technology is operational, individuals shall be required to obtain either a criminal record clearance from the Department of Justice or a criminal record exemption from the State Department of Social Services, before their initial presence in a community care facility."
  — Health & Safety Code § 1522.04(a) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1522.04(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1522.04)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Health & Safety Code § 1522.04(a), which describes live-scan technology in the specific statutory context of community care facility licensing (Health & Safety Code Chapter 3 and related chapters). It does not independently verify that identical live-scan technology or terminology governs every sector that uses DOJ fingerprint-based clearance (for example, licensing under the Business and Professions Code), though "Live Scan" is used as a general term across California licensing programs. It does not describe the fingerprinting hardware, vendor network (e.g., approved Live Scan operator locations), or processing-time standards in any further detail.

GENERAL FRAMEWORK — PENAL CODE § 11105.3
Penal Code § 11105.3 authorizes a "human resource agency or employer" to request criminal history records from the California Department of Justice for a person who applies for a license, employment, or a volunteer position in which that person would have supervisory or disciplinary power over a minor or any other person under their care. The request covers records of convictions and any arrest pending adjudication involving offenses specified in Welfare & Institutions Code § 15660(a). The Department of Justice furnishes the resulting information to the requesting employer and separately sends a copy of the same information to the applicant.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "a human resource agency or an employer may request from the Department of Justice records of all convictions or any arrest pending adjudication involving the offenses specified in subdivision (a) of Section 15660 of the Welfare and Institutions Code of a person who applies for a license, employment, or volunteer position, in which they would have supervisory or disciplinary power over a minor or any person under their care. The department shall furnish the information to the requesting employer and shall also send a copy of the information to the applicant."
  — Penal Code § 11105.3(a) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Penal Code § 11105.3(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=11105.3)
  Known gap: This clause quotes Penal Code § 11105.3(a) only. Subdivision (a) is narrower than a fully general licensing/employment background-check statute: by its own terms it applies to positions involving supervisory or disciplinary power over a minor or a person under the applicant's care, not to every regulated occupation. Subdivision (d) of the same section states that § 11105.3 does not supersede sector-specific mandatory statutes and lists several — including the childcare and community-care-facility statutes in Health & Safety Code Divisions covered partly by this document's other clauses, and Family Code and Welfare & Institutions Code provisions this document does not independently verify. This clause does not address the definitions in subdivision (f) (e.g., "human resource agency," "employer") in full, the notification-to-parents provisions in subdivision (c), or the confidentiality provisions in subdivision (g).

THE STATE DOJ ROLE VERSUS THE FEDERAL FBI ROLE
A Live Scan request under Penal Code § 11105.3 must include the applicant's fingerprints, which may be taken by the requester itself, along with any other data the Department of Justice specifies. The California Department of Justice is the entity that receives and processes the request. Separately, when a request seeks federal-level criminal history information, the Department of Justice forwards that portion of the request to the Federal Bureau of Investigation to be searched for any record of arrests or convictions. In other sector-specific statutes, this same two-tier structure recurs: fingerprint images and related information are submitted to the Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, through the Department of Justice, for a combined state and federal level criminal offender record information search.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "A request for records under subdivision (a) shall include the applicant’s fingerprints, which may be taken by the requester, and any other data specified by the department."
  — Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=11105.3)
  "Requests received by the department for federal level criminal offender record information shall be forwarded to the Federal Bureau of Investigation by the department to be searched for any record of arrests or convictions."
  — Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=11105.3)
  Known gap: This clause draws on two non-adjacent sentences within the same subdivision, Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(1) — the fingerprint-submission requirement and the federal-forwarding provision — separated in the statutory text by intervening sentences about the request form, fee, and a nonprofit fee exemption (not independently quoted here). The final sentence of this clause's body describing the state-and-federal submission structure in "other sector-specific statutes" paraphrases language independently verified in Health & Safety Code § 1596.871(a)(3)(E) and (c)(1)(A), which this document's childcare-sector clause addresses separately; it is not itself a verified quotation in this clause. This clause does not describe the FBI's own processing timeline, its separate legal authority to maintain records, or federal law (e.g., the FBI's rap-back or Compact Council authorities) governing its recordkeeping.

THE APPLICANT'S RIGHT TO A COPY AND TO CHALLENGE THE REPORT
Under Penal Code § 11105.3, the human resource agency or employer that receives a Live Scan background screening report must notify the applicant in writing of three specific rights: the right to obtain a copy of the background screening report, including any criminal history records it contains; the right to challenge the accuracy and completeness of any information the report contains; and the right to obtain a determination as to the validity of that challenge before the human resource agency or employer makes a final decision based on the criminal history information.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The human resource agency or employer shall notify the person in writing of their right to obtain a copy of any background screening report, including the criminal history records, if any, contained in the report, to challenge the accuracy and completeness of any information contained in any such report, and to obtain a determination as to the validity of such challenge before a final determination regarding the person is made by the human resource agency or employer reviewing the criminal history information."
  — Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(2)(F) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(2)(F) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=11105.3)
  Known gap: This clause quotes a single sentence, Penal Code § 11105.3(b)(2)(F). It does not describe the procedural mechanics of how a challenge is submitted, to whom, on what timeline, or how "a determination as to the validity of such challenge" is made or by whom — the statutory text quoted here does not specify a process for that determination. It also does not address the separate right, stated in some sector-specific statutes such as Health & Safety Code § 1596.871(i) and § 1265.5(k), for an individual to request a copy of the underlying state or federal criminal offender record information search response directly from the licensing department after a denial; those provisions are independent of § 11105.3(b)(2)(F) and are not quoted in this clause.

SECTOR EXAMPLE — CHILDCARE LICENSING (HEALTH & SAFETY CODE § 1596.871)
California's Child Day Care Act requires positive fingerprint identification of applicants as a condition of issuing licenses, permits, or certificates of approval to operate or provide direct care services in a childcare center or family childcare home. The statute states the Legislature's intent to require fingerprints of individuals whose contact with child day care facility clients may pose a risk to children's health and safety, and requires an individual to obtain either a criminal record clearance or a criminal record exemption from the State Department of Social Services before that individual's initial presence in a child day care facility. The statute extends this requirement beyond the license applicant to other specified persons — including staff, volunteers, and employees who have contact with the children, subject to certain stated exemptions (for example, for time-limited volunteers directly supervised and not left alone with children).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The Legislature recognizes the need to generate timely and accurate positive fingerprint identification of applicants as a condition of issuing licenses, permits, or certificates of approval for persons to operate or provide direct care services in a childcare center or family childcare home. It is the intent of the Legislature in enacting this section to require the fingerprints of those individuals whose contact with child day care facility clients may pose a risk to the children’s health and safety. An individual shall be required to obtain either a criminal record clearance or a criminal record exemption from the State Department of Social Services before the individual’s initial presence in a child day care facility."
  — Health & Safety Code § 1596.871 (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1596.871 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1596.871)
  Known gap: This clause quotes the introductory paragraph of Health & Safety Code § 1596.871. Section 1596.871 is lengthy (subdivisions (a) through (j)); this clause does not independently verify the specific disqualifying-conviction list in subdivision (a)(1), the exemption criteria and procedure in subdivision (f), the civil-penalty amounts and timelines in subdivision (c), or the fingerprint-clearance transfer provisions in subdivision (h). Health & Safety Code § 1596.871 is one of several statutes Penal Code § 11105.3(d) cross-references as a mandatory statute that § 11105.3 does not supersede; this document treats § 1596.871 as an independent, sector-specific example rather than as a subdivision of § 11105.3.

SECTOR EXAMPLE — INTERMEDIATE CARE FACILITIES FOR THE DEVELOPMENTALLY DISABLED (HEALTH & SAFETY CODE § 1265.5)
Health & Safety Code § 1265.5 requires a Department of Justice fingerprint-based criminal record clearance before licensure, renewal, or hiring of direct care staff at an intermediate care facility for the developmentally disabled (several license subtypes, including habilitative, nursing, and continuous-nursing facilities). Before initial licensure or renewal of such a facility, or upon hiring of its direct care staff, the licensing department must secure Department of Justice criminal offender record information to determine whether the applicant, facility administrator or manager, any direct care staff, or any other adult living in the same location has ever been convicted of a crime other than a minor traffic violation.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "the department shall secure from the Department of Justice criminal offender record information to determine whether the applicant, facility administrator or manager, any direct care staff, or any other adult living in the same location, has ever been convicted of a crime other than a minor traffic violation."
  — Health & Safety Code § 1265.5(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1265.5(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1265.5)
  Known gap: Section 1265.5's title places it in the Health Facilities chapter of the Health & Safety Code's licensing division, but its actual scope, as verified from the fetched text, is narrower than "healthcare facilities" generally: by its own terms it applies specifically to intermediate care facilities for the developmentally disabled (the ICF/DD license subtypes listed in subdivision (a)(1)), not to hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, or other health facility types licensed under the same chapter. This document does not verify whether a separate, differently-numbered statute imposes an equivalent Live Scan mandate on hospitals or other general acute care facilities, and it should not be read as a general statement about all healthcare licensure. This clause also does not address the specific disqualifying-conviction list in subdivision (b), the good-character/rehabilitation factors in subdivision (c), or the AFL (All Facilities Letter) processing-standard mechanism in subdivision (a)(3).

SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATION

Position: Childcare Program Assistant
Date: _______________

Acme Corp. certifies that this information sheet was provided to Jordan Lee.
